causes.what: dist-sw-02 failed or lost its uplink to core-rtr-01, cutting off app, db, cache and hv-01 hosts behind it, which in turn caused 5xx on the web tier.
The primary database volume filled up, so writes failed and the app tier threw database errors, causing 5xx at web and lb, with replica lag and queue backlog as downstream effects.
The cache is slow or degraded, so app and web response times rise and job queues back up.
dns-01 is CPU-saturated and resolves names slowly, making app and web responses slow.
nas-01 has high storage latency, which slows the db-01 disk I/O (its storage is on nas-01), so queries are slow and connections pile up, slowing app and web.
app-03 has an application-level problem (slow responses with a growing job queue), such as a bad process or a job backlog, local to that host.

unrelated_alerts: web-02: Disk space is low on /

causes.what: A bad application deploy (the version changed on app-02) caused database errors on the app hosts, so the web tier returned 5xx.
The core router has a high interface error rate, such as a bad link or optic, causing packet loss across all hosts, with web-03 then going fully unreachable.

db-02 is overloaded (high CPU, slow queries, replication lag), possibly from a heavy query, and its reads are slowing the app and web tiers. A cache hit ratio drop on cache-01 may be a cold or flushed cache that pushes load onto the database.
The cache has a low hit ratio, which sends extra read load to the database.

Backend web servers failed their health checks or were taken out of the load balancer pool (fewer than 2 healthy), though no web alerts exist, so this is probably a health-check or config issue or a backend outage with no alert.
